source_refs.note: The Product Rule of Probability: a main subheading of 18.2.2 Inheritance and Mathematical Probabilities, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 89-89.

blocks.text: The product rule of probability says that the chance of two or more independent events happening together is calculated by multiplying their individual probabilities. For example, getting a six on one dice is 1/6. For two dice, the chance of getting two sixes is (1/6) × (1/6) = 1/36.
The product rule can be used to predict fertilization outcomes.

blocks.title: Example 1 (Aa × Aa):
steps: Each parent has a 1/2 chance of giving gamete with allele a.

blocks.title: Example 2 (RrYy × RrYy):
steps: Probability of Round seed = 3/4, Probability of yellow seed = 3/4.
blocks.answer: So, probability of round yellow offspring = (3/4) × (3/4) = 9/16.
